sourceEvidence.label: Remote PC/CIFS disclosure, retained helpers, persistence analysis, and offline verification records

assessment.summary: The evidence supports replacing the stringly root CIFS command boundary with typed, shell-free mount and unmount operations; writable boot-consumer integrity is a complementary control.

nonNegotiables: Preserve supported SMB credentials and share names, including valid spaces, Unicode, and punctuation.
Remove shell interpretation from both mount and unmount paths.
Do not add a reusable privileged-access mechanism.
Keep target identity, authorization phrases, and owner-specific payloads private.
assumptions: No measured performance, memory, or availability budget was supplied.
The first affected release, model range, and vendor-fixed release are unknown.
Exact on-device replaceability of boot-consumed /opt paths remains unresolved.

opportunities.title: Make privileged CIFS operations typed and shell-free
opportunities.summary: Own parsing, credential handling, target policy, and process creation at one privileged boundary instead of reparsing caller data as a shell program.
opportunities.diagnosis: Mount and unmount each receive a command-shaped string, perform substitutions after caller validation, and delegate interpretation to a root shell. That ownership split lets lower-trust data become code and makes lifecycle validation drift between the two operations.

evidence.claim: One credential-derived command executed as UID 0 through the mount path on the assessed device.
The retained mount helper substitutes credential and share values into a root bash -c command.
The retained unmount helper independently substitutes the share value into root bash -c.
Enabled consumers of persistent /opt content could turn an arbitrary root write into post-reboot execution if exact runtime paths are replaceable.
The owner reports a one-shot defensive replacement, without an independent live transcript or current device readback in this task.

desiredInvariants: Remote PC and credential-file values remain data through process creation.
The privileged component selects a fixed executable and a fixed option schema.
Credentials remain in a protected out-of-band channel and do not enter shell text, logs, or unintended process arguments.
Mount and disconnect validate the same canonical target and credential lifecycle.
Valid SMB character space is preserved independently of shell syntax.
Boot-critical content on persistent storage is authenticity-checked or not writable by the CIFS service context.

options.title: Repair the existing helpers with direct argv
options.summary: Keep the current service and scripts, but parse fixed fields, retain credentials out of band, and invoke mount and unmount directly without a shell.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Removing shell evaluation blocks the demonstrated mount route.
The vulnerable mount helper is directly replaced.
The equivalent unmount sink is directly replaced.
The observed entry point can no longer write through a shell, but boot-consumer integrity remains separate.

tradeoffs.assessment: Direct execution removes shell parsing from both observed helpers, though future script call sites can recreate the pattern.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run the bounded regression corpus through mount and disconnect and verify no shell child is created.

tradeoffs.assessment: Eliminating a shell process should remove one fork and parse step; the mount operation still dominates latency.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare end-to-end mount and disconnect latency over at least 100 local-lab iterations.

tradeoffs.assessment: Removing the transient shell should modestly reduce peak process memory, with no retained state added.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure peak RSS and process count during representative mount and disconnect operations.

tradeoffs.assessment: Arguments stop depending on shell tokenization, but script parsing and duplicated mount/unmount logic remain failure sources.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise success, authentication failure, cancellation, stale credential files, and disconnect cleanup.

tradeoffs.assessment: No new daemon or protocol is introduced; structured rejection telemetry should be added to existing logs.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Confirm support logs identify field and policy failures without exposing credentials.

tradeoffs.assessment: This is the smallest image change and can preserve the current caller contract, but scripts remain a long-term maintenance boundary.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run the existing Remote PC compatibility matrix and perform image rollback to the prior helper set.

residualRisks: Other privileged helpers can repeat the command-string pattern.
Duplicated parsing between mount and unmount can drift.
Enabled boot consumers of writable persistent content remain architectural risk.

workPackages: Replace string evaluation with direct argv and protected credential handling.
Unify canonical target and credential-file lifecycle checks.
Add compatibility and adversarial regression cases.
acceptanceCriteria: Valid supported SMB values retain their literal meaning.
Mount and disconnect cleanup pass success and failure tests.
migrationNotes: Ship mount and unmount changes in the same firmware image.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Restore the prior signed image, not individual unverified helper bytes.

options.title: Replace the string method with a typed privileged API
options.summary: Move parsing, option policy, credential lifetime, mount identifiers, and direct process creation into one owned privileged component.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: The demonstrated string-to-shell edge is removed; direct helper repair is still needed during migration.
Credential data no longer enters a command string.
Disconnect uses a returned mount identifier rather than reparsing share data.
The entry primitive is removed, while boot-path integrity still requires its own work.

tradeoffs.assessment: One component owns schema validation and process creation, eliminating command strings and reducing policy drift between mount and disconnect.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Fuzz the typed decoder, verify fixed executable selection, and replay the full adversarial corpus end to end.

tradeoffs.assessment: Typed serialization adds bounded parsing but removes shell startup; SMB and mount I/O should dominate, but no measurements exist.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure p50, p95, and p99 mount and disconnect latency against the repaired-helper baseline.

tradeoffs.assessment: Bounded request objects and a small mount-state table replace transient shell state; retained mount identifiers require explicit limits.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure steady and peak RSS with zero, one, and maximum supported concurrent shares.

tradeoffs.assessment: A returned mount identifier and single cleanup owner remove reconstruction and stale-file ambiguity, but protocol-version skew must fail safely.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Test restart recovery, duplicate requests, cancellation, stale identifiers, partial mounts, and service-version mismatch.

tradeoffs.assessment: Structured error codes and redacted audit events improve supportability, while the API requires ownership and version observability.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run incident exercises using only redacted service logs and confirm each failure class is distinguishable.

tradeoffs.assessment: Launcher, client library, privileged service, and tests must move together or support an explicitly bounded compatibility period.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Test mixed-version failure behavior and staged rollout, with downgrade blocked once the old method is removed.

residualRisks: Decoder, canonicalization, and kernel mount interfaces remain privileged attack surfaces.
A compatibility shim could retain the old command-string risk if not time-bounded.
Boot-consumed writable content requires separate integrity hardening.

workPackages: Define a versioned typed request and response schema.
Implement canonical target and fixed option policy in the privileged service.
Return opaque mount identifiers for disconnect.
Retire command-shaped helper methods after compatibility rollout.
acceptanceCriteria: No CIFS request contains a caller-selected executable, raw option string, or credential value.
Disconnect needs only an opaque service-issued identifier.
Mixed-version and rollback behavior fail closed without orphaning mounts.
migrationNotes: Deploy the direct-argv helper repair before or with the first typed client.
Instrument old-method use and remove the method after one bounded release window.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Rollback the full signed client/service image pair while retaining the direct-argv tactical fix.

options.title: Put CIFS mounting in an isolated broker
options.summary: Use a narrowly privileged process or service with a typed protocol, constrained filesystem view, fixed executable, and bounded mount namespace.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: The broker has no shell-evaluation path; the existing helpers still need repair until cutover.
The vulnerable helper is removed from the active path.
Unmount is broker-owned and keyed by broker state.
Confinement can deny writes to boot-consumed /opt paths even if the broker is compromised.

tradeoffs.assessment: A reduced label, namespace, and filesystem view can contain parser or mount-helper failures beyond this injection, assuming the platform enforces those controls.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Test denied access to boot paths, executable substitution, unrelated devices, network destinations, and ambient capabilities.

tradeoffs.assessment: A broker adds one IPC hop and request serialization; mount I/O may hide the cost, but frequent reconnects could expose it.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Benchmark cold and warm mounts, reconnect storms, and maximum supported concurrent shares.

tradeoffs.assessment: A resident broker, state table, and IPC buffers add bounded steady memory.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Set an explicit RSS and per-mount state budget, then measure idle and peak use.

tradeoffs.assessment: Failure isolation improves, but broker restart, namespace ownership, and orphaned-mount recovery create new state transitions.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inject crashes at every operation boundary and verify deterministic recovery without leaked mounts or credentials.

tradeoffs.assessment: The new service needs health, policy, audit, crash, and lifecycle observability plus incident runbooks.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise upgrade, restart, policy denial, and degraded-service runbooks on representative devices.

tradeoffs.assessment: This changes deployment, labels, IPC, mount ownership, and recovery semantics across multiple firmware components.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Use a staged signed-image rollout with a kill switch and full-image rollback rehearsal.

residualRisks: The broker and its protocol become a new privileged security boundary.
Incorrect namespace propagation or label policy can break Shared Folder behavior.
Isolation does not replace input schema validation or boot-content integrity checks.

workPackages: Threat-model broker authority and namespace propagation.
Implement the typed protocol and minimum capability set.
Add crash recovery, redacted audit, and resource bounds.
Migrate callers and remove old privileged methods.
acceptanceCriteria: Broker compromise cannot modify boot-consumed /opt content or execute arbitrary programs.
Crash recovery leaves no credential files or unowned mounts.
Shared Folder remains compatible across the supported matrix.
migrationNotes: Use only if platform containment can be validated on the product kernel and policy set.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Rollback the complete signed broker/client/policy image while retaining the direct-argv tactical repair.

opportunities.recommendation: Use direct-argv helpers immediately, then move to a typed privileged API as the vendor-grade design. Choose an isolated broker only when broader containment justifies its lifecycle and resource costs.

openQuestions: Which SMB character, length, and Unicode-normalization rules are contractual across all supported clients?
What credential-file or file-descriptor interface is supported by the shipped CIFS stack?
When exactly does disconnect run, and what owns credential deletion on every path?
Which /opt consumers are present, writable, label-compatible, and integrity-checked on representative devices?
What signed-image rollout and mixed-version compatibility window can Samsung support?
